title: The NLstart2run study: Incidence and risk factors of running-related injuries in novice runners
authors: Kluitenberg B, van Middelkoop M, Smits DW, Verhagen E, Hartgens F, Diercks R, van der Worp H
journal: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
population: Adults aged 18-65 in a 6-week supervised 'Start to Run' program in the Netherlands
findings: 1696 runners were included; 10.9% sustained an RRI during the 6-week program.
RRI was defined as a musculoskeletal complaint of the lower extremity or back attributed to running that hampered running ability for three consecutive training sessions.
Multivariable Cox regression: higher age, higher BMI, previous musculoskeletal complaints not attributed to sports, and no previous running experience were related to RRI.
The authors recommend using the identified risk factors for screening and prevention.
limitations: Short 6-week follow-up of a supervised program; self-reported weekly log; the abstract gives no effect sizes or thresholds for the risk factors.
implications: Raise a novice's baseline injury-risk flag for higher age, higher BMI, recent non-sport musculoskeletal complaints, or no running history; for flagged runners slow the first weeks and use more walk intervals (action choice is a design decision, not tested here).
Add an intake screen for age, BMI, prior musculoskeletal complaints and running experience; no numeric cut-offs are justified by this abstract.

verification.notes: Own re-fetch: Crossref first author Kluitenberg, 7 authors, SJMSS, issued 2014-12 online, 2015 in Europe PMC. Abstract matches all numbers and definitions. Removed the researcher's '6-12 weeks' interpretation as a finding.
